chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli from Abdullah ibn Sulayman said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted broadened the provisions of the foolish so that the wise may take lesson from them and know that what is in this world is not attained by effort nor by stratagem.'

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life, the lower realm
key_terms.الْحُمْقَى: The foolish, those lacking deep wisdom or spiritual insight
key_terms.الْعُقَلاَءُ: The wise, those with intellect and spiritual discernment

ai.seo_question: Why does God give wealth to the foolish according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the prosperity of the foolish, serving as a lesson for the wise to recognize that worldly success is not strictly tied to human effort or intellect. This concept underscores the Shia understanding of *barakah* and divine grace (*fadl*), reminding believers that material wealth is a test rather than a definitive indicator of spiritual merit. It encourages detachment from worldly metrics of success and fosters humility, knowing that God distributes provisions according to His wisdom, not merely human capability.
